emerging_technology: LLM-based generative AI customer-service assistant using retrieval from an internal enterprise knowledge base.
intended_application: Draft replies for order inquiries, returns policies, and common after-sales questions. A human customer-service representative must review and approve each draft before sending. No autonomous sending, refunds, account changes, or policy exceptions. Current order status must come from an authorized order system checked by the human reviewer; the knowledge base is not a source of live order status.
industry_sector: Hypothetical mid-sized e-commerce retailer of ordinary consumer goods; jurisdiction and specific legal obligations are not specified and must not be invented.
business_need: Assess whether assisted drafting can reduce total customer-service handling effort and operating costs while maintaining reply accuracy and customer trust. No measured savings or baseline performance are supplied.
users_stakeholders: Customer-service representatives, customers, customer-service manager, knowledge-base maintainers, IT/security and privacy reviewers, and management responsible for the decision.
risk_consequence_context: Hypothetical risks include incorrect returns commitments, inaccurate order information, disclosure of customer data, inconsistent policy interpretation, and loss of trust. Human approval does not guarantee error detection. Draft generation can be stopped and staff can return to manual replies, but messages already sent and data already disclosed cannot necessarily be reversed. The underlying tasks and potential harms are held constant across cases.
management_question: Should this organization start a limited pilot of this application within the next three months? Select a defensible adoption posture, scope and conditions from the permitted recommendation set, or request critical missing evidence. Do not assume pilot approval or expand the decision into immediate full deployment.
time_horizon: The three months following the assessment date. No fixed pilot duration or deployment date has been approved.
additional_context: All organizational attributes and workflow boundaries in this case are hypothetical test assumptions, not observed company facts. No technology evidence, actual test results, vendor selection, numerical performance thresholds, approved budget, data-processing permission, or legal clearance is provided. Use the same verified and dated external evidence packet for both cases when available; if absent, flag the evidence gap. Compare the existing human workflow and simpler search/template improvements. Do not presume the final recommendation. This contrast changes multiple organizational conditions, so it tests context sensitivity rather than isolating the causal effect of risk tolerance alone.
organization: Hypothetical Company A, a mid-sized e-commerce retailer; this is not a real company.
adoption_posture: Moderately proactive and willing to learn through a limited, reversible test, while requiring evidence of value and appropriate risk controls.
capabilities_constraints: Hypothetical assumptions for review: an existing internal policy knowledge base has a designated owner and a regular update process, but its accuracy and completeness have not yet been audited for this application. A customer-service lead can coordinate reviewers and a limited evaluation; reviewer competence and workload remain unmeasured. A scoped pilot proposal can be considered through the normal management and IT/security review process; no approval is presumed. De-identified historical or synthetic cases can be prepared for offline evaluation, subject to checking that de-identification is adequate. Integration feasibility, vendor terms, costs, privacy requirements, and actual production data access remain unknown.
